body:
`theme:sector-private-banks` · confidence: single-source · tickers: HDFCBANK, ICICIBANK, KOTAKBANK, AXISBANK, INDUSINDBK

**How it makes money:** Spread lending + fee income; liability (CASA) franchise is the moat.

**Metrics that matter:**
- NIM
- CASA ratio / cost of funds
- credit cost
- GNPA/NNPA, slippage ratio
- PCR
- RoA
- CD ratio
- CET1

**Value chain and where margins sit:** Deposits (cheap retail CASA = margin) -> underwriting -> collections. Margins are highest in unsecured retail, cards and MSME, and lowest in corporate. Fee pools come from distribution (insurance, MF) and payments.

**Cycle drivers:** Repo/EBLR repricing, system liquidity, credit/deposit growth gap, unsecured retail and MSME stress, RBI risk weights (Nov 2023 hike on unsecured).

**Lead indicators (public India data):**
- RBI sectoral deployment of bank credit (monthly)
- RBI fortnightly scheduled bank statement (credit/deposit growth)
- CRIF/TransUnion CIBIL delinquency reports
- RBI Financial Stability Report (Jun/Dec)
- SMA book disclosures in results

**What separated winners from losers:** Winners: deposit-led growth, low CD ratio, steady RoA through cycles, conservative provisioning, management continuity. Losers: loan growth well above deposit growth, concentrated corporate or group exposures, evergreening, governance and accounting surprises (Yes Bank 2018–20; IndusInd 2025).

**Valuation ranges and peaks/troughs:** P/B vs sustainable RoE (justified P/B = (RoE-g)/(CoE-g)). Quality private banks ~3–5x P/B in the 2014–21 peak era, de-rated to ~2–2.5x by 2024–26. Troughs: 2008–09, 2013 taper tantrum, Mar 2020. Nifty Bank 1.63x P/B / 12.1x P/E on 27 Oct 2026; Bank P/E 14.4 vs 7-yr median 17.4 (Jun 2026).

**Current state (Nov 2026):** System credit ~18.1% vs deposits ~17.3% YoY (mid-Sep 2026); non-food credit +18.8% (31 Aug 2026, RBI). HDFC Bank Q2 FY27 NIM 3.16% (Q1 3.26%), credit cost 0.44%, standalone PAT +4.7%. Private-bank NIMs are down ~8–20 bps as costlier term and FCNR deposits fund growth, and PSBs lead on profit growth.

**Classic traps:**
- Low P/B is not cheap if RoA is structurally falling
- Loan growth funded by bulk or term deposits
- Stage-2 or restructured books hidden in 'other'
- Assuming merger synergies (HDFC–HDFC Bank margin dilution lasted 2023–26)
- Ignoring the CEO-succession and RBI-tenure overhang

`case_study:alkyl-amines-2009-2021` · tickers: ALKYLAMINE · confidence: single-source

Split-adjusted ₹7.81 (Feb 2009) → ATH ₹4,386 (Jul 2021) ≈560x; standalone P/E 8.4 → 76 (9x) × implied EPS ~62x. Final leg ₹315 (Jan 2019) → ₹4,386: 14x in 2.6 years with EPS ~3.6x (₹16.2 → ₹58.1) and P/E 18.6 → 76 (4x). Drawdowns in the run: −35% (2014–15), −29% (COVID). Early signal (narrative partly unverified): India's leading methyl/ethyl-amine maker, import-substituting Chinese supply. Visible in filings: steady capacity additions; FY21 standalone OPM 35% and ROCE 56% as amine spreads widened during Chinese environmental shutdowns and COVID pharma demand; for a decade before that it traded at P/E 5–17. Ended: spreads normalised and domestic competition added capacity; standalone EPS FY21 ₹57.9 → FY24 ₹29.1 (−50%) and revenue −14% in FY24. The stock fell −71% to ₹1,278 (Mar 2026); ₹1,573 on 19 Nov 2026 (P/E ~32), with EPS partly recovered (TTM ₹48). Lesson: a peak-spread year capitalised at 76x is a classic cyclical top. For chemicals, ask what EPS looks like at mid-cycle spreads before paying a quality multiple.

Key data: **start_year**: 2009; **end_year**: 2021; **start_price**: 7.81; **end_price**: 4386; **price_nov2026**: 1573; **multiple**: ~560x (14x in 2019-21); **pe_start**: 8.4; **pe_end**: 75.7; **eps_multiple_implied**: ~62x; **max_drawdown**: -35% in run; -71% after; **early_signals**: import substitution; capacity adds; P/E 5-17 for a decade; **ended**: spread normalisation FY22-24; **lesson**: don't capitalise peak spreads at 75x

Sources: <https://www.screener.in/company/ALKYLAMINE/>

body:
`insight:buffett-leverage-99-to-1` | confidence: verified | date: 1990-03-02

1989 letter: higher (still conventional) leverage would have lifted Berkshire's 23.8% average ROE, and 'perhaps we could have judged there to be a 99% probability that higher leverage would lead to nothing but good' - yet a 1% chance of 'temporary anguish and default' is unacceptable: 'We wouldn't have liked those 99:1 odds - and never will. A small chance of distress or disgrace cannot, in our view, be offset by a large chance of extra returns. If your actions are sensible, you are certain to get good results; in most such cases, leverage just moves things along faster.' 1990: banks at 20:1 leverage magnify managerial errors, so 'we have no interest in purchasing shares of a poorly-managed bank at a "cheap" price.' 2014 letter: investors make stocks risky through 'Active trading, attempts to "time" market movements, inadequate diversification, the payment of high and unnecessary fees ... and the use of borrowed money'; 'borrowed money has no place in the investor's tool kit: Anything can happen anytime in markets'; 'Market forecasters will fill your ear but will never fill your wallet.' 2025 (Abel): balance sheet as 'a strategic asset to be deployed at the right time', cash+T-bills over $370bn. Actionable for an Indian individual: no margin/MTF, no F&O for leverage (ties to SEBI F&O loss study); in companies, prefer net-cash or low-debt compounders; for lenders demand best-in-class management.

Sources:
- https://www.berkshirehathaway.com/letters/1989.html
- https://www.berkshirehathaway.com/letters/1990.html
- https://www.berkshirehathaway.com/letters/2014ltr.pdf
- https://www.berkshirehathaway.com/letters/2025ltr.pdf

We expect medium-term EBITDA Margin to be within the current guided range of 22% to 24%.' Screener OPM: Mar-25 24%, Sep-25 24%, Dec-25 23%, Mar-26 23%, Jun-26 23%, Sep-26 22% — steady downward drift.

- **Base-rate reasoning:** HUL's quarterly EBITDA margin has stayed ≥22% in essentially every quarter of the last ~3 years (~85%).

1. **OS:** Raspberry Pi OS **64-bit** (Bookworm or newer). Pi 4/5 with ≥4 GB RAM. Use an SSD over USB if you can,
   because SD cards wear out with constant database writes. Set timezone: `sudo timedatectl set-timezone Asia/Kolkata`.
2. **Packages:**
   `sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y git python3 python3-venv poppler-utils sqlite3 curl nodejs npm`
3. **Repo:** `mkdir -p ~/fein-lab && cd ~/fein-lab && git clone https://github.com/aditya-bad/fein.git && cd fein && git checkout claude/focused-brahmagupta-g3hraq`
   (needs a GitHub login with access to the repo, for example a fine-grained token with access to this one repo only.)
4. **Data folder:** `mkdir -p ~/fein-data` (the nightly collectors write here).
5. **Connecting it to me (Remote Control).** The Claude desktop app doesn't run on a Pi, so use Claude Code in a terminal:
   - Install Claude Code on the Pi (`curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash`), then run `claude` once and log in with **your** account.
   - In the folder to share, run: `cd ~/fein-lab && claude remote-control`. Keep it running (for example in `tmux`, or as a systemd service).
   - Tell me when it's running. I'll check whether this cloud session can see the folder and request access; you approve on the Pi.
   - Honest caveat: using a computer's folder from a cloud session isn't available on every account yet. If I can't see it,
     you can still run a Claude session **on the Pi itself**, which reads this same repo, memory and all.
6. **Cron jobs** (I'll give the exact lines when the detector scripts are ready in `tools/detectors/README.md`). They run without
   Claude, so they cost none of my usage.
7. **Gemini CLI:** `sudo npm install -g @google/gemini-cli`, then run `gemini` once and log in. Check `gemini -p "say ok"` prints a reply.
